title: Water - 123 school
heading: Water
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Name the four functions of water
questions.a: Drinking water, solvent, rinsing agent and help in food preparation

questions.q: What is a rinsing agent?
questions.a: A liquid that washes away other substances

questions.q: What is surface water?
questions.a: Water on the surface of the Earth, such as rivers, lakes and oceans

questions.q: What is groundwater?
questions.a: Water that is in the soil, underground

questions.q: Is drinking water a pure substance?
questions.a: No, substances are dissolved in it, such as lime

questions.q: What is distilled water?
questions.a: Pure water, without dissolved substances

questions.q: Which water usually contains less pollution: groundwater or surface water?
questions.a: Groundwater

questions.q: Which water contains the highest concentration of salts?
questions.a: Seawater

questions.q: What is the density of seawater? (use BINAS table 16)
questions.a: 1.02 g/cm<sup>3</sup> (distilled water: 1.00 g/cm<sup>3</sup>)

questions.q: Seawater contains a lot of table salt (sodium chloride, Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup>). Is table salt very soluble, slightly soluble or insoluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
questions.a: Very soluble

questions.q: Less water flows in a river. The amount of pollution stays the same. What happens to the concentration?
questions.a: The concentration becomes higher

questions.q: What does disinfecting mean?
questions.a: Making pathogens harmless

questions.q: What function does water have when it keeps an engine or a factory cool?
questions.a: Coolant

questions.q: What is a coolant?
questions.a: A substance that absorbs heat and carries it away

questions.q: Why is water so suitable as a coolant?
questions.a: Water can absorb a lot of heat and is cheap and widely available

questions.q: What is industrial water?
questions.a: Water that factories use, for example for cooling or cleaning. It does not need to be of drinking-water quality

questions.q: What function does water have when you cook pasta?
questions.a: Help in food preparation

questions.q: What function does water have when you rinse dirty pans?
questions.a: Rinsing agent

questions.q: What is a solvent?
questions.a: A substance in which you can dissolve another substance

questions.q: What is a solution?
questions.a: A clear mixture of a dissolved substance in a solvent

questions.q: You dissolve salt in water. What is the solute and what is the solvent?
questions.a: Salt is the solute, water is the solvent

questions.q: From which two kinds of water does a drinking-water company in the Netherlands mainly make drinking water?
questions.a: Groundwater and surface water

questions.q: Why does surface water have to be purified before you can drink it?
questions.a: It contains dirt, bacteria and dissolved substances

questions.q: What is the first step in purifying surface water?
questions.a: Removing coarse dirt with grids and sieves

questions.q: What does a drinking-water company use a sand filter for?
questions.a: To filter small solid particles out of the water

questions.q: What is the filtrate when you let water run through a sand filter?
questions.a: The water that passes through the filter. The dirt that stays behind is called the residue

questions.q: What is activated carbon used for in the purification of water?
questions.a: Odour and flavour substances stay attached to the carbon (adsorption)

questions.q: On which property is adsorption with activated carbon based?
questions.a: Tendency to attach to a surface: some substances attach better to the surface of the carbon than others

questions.q: Why is drinking water disinfected?
questions.a: To make bacteria and other pathogens harmless

questions.q: How can you make drinking water from seawater?
questions.a: By distilling: the water evaporates and the salt stays behind

questions.q: What is the distillate when you distil seawater?
questions.a: Pure water

questions.q: How can you get salt out of seawater?
questions.a: By evaporating the water: the water evaporates and the salt remains

questions.q: Why is seawater not suitable for drinking?
questions.a: It contains too many dissolved salts

questions.q: Why is a factory not allowed to simply discharge waste water into a river?
questions.a: The waste water pollutes the surface water

questions.q: What happens to waste water in a sewage treatment plant?
questions.a: It is purified before it goes back into the surface water
